The Monsters exposes the humanity that exists under the perceived ruthlessness within a brutal profession, but its core strength lies in its exploration of family bonds.
Surprises might be few, but The Monsters is a fine study of two siblings who refuse to be beaten down and find communion in the fight.
Though it falters in its final act, Anyanwu’s The Monsters is a showcase of Mizzelle and Onaodowan’s range and talent.
The Monsters is a rare fusion of muscular physicality and emotional depth, a production that hits hard in every sense and earns every one of its bruises.
The Monsters is a layered, emotionally muscular play powered by two formidable performances and technical flair that matches a script full of duels and drama alike.
This is a powerful play of love and forgiveness set within the parameters of a boxing ring.

The Monsters delivers a bruising, brilliant exploration of sibling trauma that lands nearly every emotional punch.
